objective: Build a versioned AI orientation/onboarding system so a context-free LLM can be briefed on Rhino CHATGPT as if receiving an employee handbook, role guide, and current shift brief.
instructions: Work only in /Users/nes/bin/mcp/rhino-cad-mcp and use the normal operator.sh lifecycle.

Design the onboarding system around three layers: a stable universal handbook, role-specific guidance, and a generated current-state brief. The result must work for both remote/chat controllers and local machine operators.

Create a root-level AI_ORIENTATION.md as the canonical universal handbook. It must explain, concisely but completely: project mission; architecture; controller/GitHub/operator/Rhino roles; source-of-truth rules; normal request/branch/report lifecycle; one-command operator flow; what the controller is responsible for; what the local operator is responsible for; safety invariants; evidence/validation expectations; merge/review model; failure/blocker behavior; and a first-5-minutes checklist for a context-free AI.

Create .bridge/orientation/manifest.json with an orientation_version, compatible protocol_version, canonical handbook path, role guide paths, generated payload format/version, required live-state sources, and explicit precedence order for conflicting instructions.

Create .bridge/orientation/controller.md for ChatGPT Web or any remote/controller LLM. It must teach how to inspect repository state, write structured requests, review operator reports/evidence, verify commit/branch isolation, merge only reviewed work, and avoid pretending it has local machine/Rhino access when it does not.

Create .bridge/orientation/operator.md for Codex/Claude/local LLMs. It must teach how to sync main, use operator.sh/exchange.sh, treat request JSON as authoritative, work on operator branches, preserve local work, validate before push, write work + receipt commits, and avoid bypassing safeguards.

Create .bridge/orientation/quickstart.md containing a minimal context-free onboarding sequence. It should tell a new AI how to determine whether it is acting as controller, operator, or reviewer and what exact files to read next.

Create a root-level executable orient.sh that generates a single self-contained orientation payload suitable for pasting into a brand-new AI conversation. Supported roles must be controller, operator, reviewer, and universal. Default to universal.
orient.sh must support --copy on macOS using pbcopy when available, while still printing to stdout unless an explicit --copy-only option is chosen. It must not require third-party packages.

The generated payload must include: orientation version; repository/protocol identity; the universal handbook; selected role guide; current controller state; current main commit; and a short live-state section showing pending task count/IDs if determinable from bridge_cli.py. It must clearly label generated/live facts versus stable handbook content.
Add a small standard-library-only .bridge/orientation/build_payload.py if useful. Prefer deterministic composition from tracked files rather than duplicating handbook prose inside shell code.

Add an AGENTS.md at repository root that acts as a thin bootstrap for Codex/generic coding agents: instruct it to read AI_ORIENTATION.md and the operator role guide before substantive work, then preserve existing project-specific safety rules.

Update CLAUDE.md minimally so its existing Rhino CAD Agent Rules remain intact, but prepend or add an onboarding pointer to AI_ORIENTATION.md and .bridge/orientation/operator.md. Do not erase or weaken current rules.
Do not modify Rhino/MCP runtime implementation files: server.py, bridge.py, runtime_ops.py, tool_support.py, snippets.py, test_bridge.py, requirements.txt, knowledge/, or tests/.
Do not change operator.sh, exchange.sh, or .bridge/bridge_cli.py unless a concrete orientation-generation requirement cannot be met otherwise. If changed, document why and keep it control-plane-only.

Validate: bash -n orient.sh; python3 -m py_compile .bridge/orientation/build_payload.py if present; ./orient.sh universal; ./orient.sh controller; ./orient.sh operator; ./orient.sh reviewer; verify each payload contains the correct handbook, role guide, protocol version, repository identity, current main SHA, and controller state; git diff --check.
Do not invoke pbcopy during automated validation unless safely checking command existence; avoid mutating the user's clipboard during tests.

Create .bridge/evidence/bridge-phase10-001/orientation-system.json documenting the final file map, orientation_version, supported roles, payload contract, precedence model, validation results, and any limitations.
Commit the onboarding implementation and evidence as the work commit and capture RESULT_COMMIT.

Create .bridge/reports/bridge-phase10-001.json using the v0.3 report schema with ack exactly BRIDGE-PHASE10-20260924-ORIENT-6A2F91-OPERATOR-ACK, exact base_commit, RESULT_COMMIT, and branch operator/bridge-phase10-001.
Run python3 .bridge/bridge_cli.py verify-report bridge-phase10-001 and require REPORT_OK.
Commit the report as the separate receipt commit, push operator/bridge-phase10-001, and do not merge it.
expected_outputs: Minimal onboarding pointer update to CLAUDE.md
constraints: Orientation content must be repo-grounded and must not invent machine capabilities.
Stable handbook content and generated live state must be clearly separated.
No live Rhino tests or dependency installation.
No dangerous Git operations, force push, or merge.
Do not duplicate large handbook text across multiple files when composition can reference canonical sources.
